intended_object: The canonical comparison bifunctor ho(X) × ho(Y) → ho(X × Y), in curried form, for 2-truncated simplicial sets X, Y. It sends (x, y) to (x, y) and edges to the corresponding product edges. It is the inverse of the equivalence ho(X ⊗ Y) ≌ ho(X) × ho(Y). Inferred from the docstring, the module doc, and its use in `inverse` and `equivalence`.
explanation: The body sends objects (x, y) to mk (x, y). An edge e : y₀ → y₁ goes to the class of the product edge (id x, e). An edge e : x₀ → x₁ goes to the natural transformation with components (e, id y). The relations hold via products of 2-simplices (CompStruct.tensor), and naturality is the `square` lemma. This is the standard construction of the comparison functor hoX × hoY → ho(X × Y), here curried. The library confirms it is correct by proving that `functor ⋙ inverse` and `inverse ⋙ functor` are identities, where `inverse` is the uncurried form. The setting of 2-truncated simplicial sets is the natural one for this homotopy category construction. Mathlib has no more general version; the closest declaration is its uncurried form `inverse` in the same file. The definition is also partly an auxiliary step toward `equivalence`, but it denotes a genuine canonical functor, and it does so correctly.
